name: Warmers
label: Dischord
lede: The kid slumped on the cover of the first Minor Threat EP grew up, took up guitar, and built a trio that treated silence as a member of the band.

eras.title: A rhythm section and a singer with a guitar
eras.text: Alec MacKaye had sung for three DC bands, the Untouchables, Faith and Ignition. This time he picked up a guitar and went looking for a rhythm section that knew when to lay out.

years.cap: Alec MacKaye, Juan Luis Carrera and Amy Farina playing as the Warmers, 1994-97
years.h: Alec MacKaye starts a band with Amy Farina and Juan Luis Carrera
years.p: [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]] had heard [[Amy Farina|30d1b9a6-4156-49ec-84ba-65c3f5ebbf69]] and bassist Juan Luis Carrera play together as a rhythm section. By July 1994 the three were the Warmers, and Dischord dates the band from there.
years.xp:
Dischord says MacKaye had seen Farina's band, Mr. Candy Eater, and had heard the pair as the rhythm section behind another artist. The Collapsar puts that record as a 7" by Lois and Alec MacKaye, with Farina and Carrera on it.

MacKaye was already a known face. The kid slumped on the cover of [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]'s first EP, and on the [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]]' Minor Disturbance, is Alec.

Dischord's bio states the plan: open space, with silence treated as an instrument on equal footing with bass, guitar, drums and voice.

years.h: Thin Air 7" is the Warmers' first record
years.p: Dischord No. 100.5 has two songs, Thin Air and Occupation: Fish, the second a tribute to baseball player Roberto Clemente. It is out of print.
years.xp: The Collapsar calls Occupation: Fish the band's paean to Clemente. Dischord lists the single as 1995.

eras.title: Late arrivals
eras.text: The Warmers made one album, Warmers, at Inner Ear with Ian MacKaye, and then spent a lot of time in a van. Farina's drumming, which held off where a drummer is supposed to hit, is what people talked about.

years.h: One album, fourteen songs, Dischord No. 102
years.p: Warmers was recorded at Inner Ear and produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and the band. Snake Charmer, The Lowdown and Poked It With a Stick show the method: clipped songs with gaps left in.
years.xp:
Critics picked out the minimalism and, above all, Farina's drums. Asked about her playing, Alec MacKaye pointed to "the not-drumming in her drumming," where she doesn't hit where she's supposed to, holds off, then comes in.

The LP and CD are out of print; the songs survive as a Dischord digital release.

years.h: Sonic Youth and Blonde Redhead share bills with the Warmers
years.p: Dischord's bio says the Warmers toured the US extensively with both bands. Footage survives of a June 1996 set in New York.
years.xp: The clip is a partial set, filed as 27 June 1996 in New York. Dischord doesn't date the touring itself, and it gives no tour dates.

years.h: Sicily, 1997: the only show the Warmers play in Europe
years.p: A festival in Sicily is the band's one European date.

years.h: Three and a half years in, the Warmers stop
years.p: Dischord dates the run July 1994 to December 1997, and says the band's creative chemistry had begun to wind down.

eras.title: Wanted: more
eras.text: The Warmers came back only on record, once on 20 Years of Dischord and once with a shelved session, Wanted: More. The members kept playing in other bands.

years.h: Poked It With a Stick goes into Dischord's anniversary box
years.p: The song is on 20 Years of Dischord, Dischord No. 125.

years.cap: Amy Farina onstage with the Evens, Washington, 2007
years.h: Eight years on, the December 1996 session finally comes out
years.p: Six songs cut at Pirate House sat on a shelf until Dischord released them in May 2004 as Wanted: More, No. 144.
years.xp: Alec MacKaye, the band and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] mixed the session. It has Red Light Runner, Totally Free and Berretta USA.

years.h: Farina and MacKaye keep going: The Evens, Coriky, Hammered Hulls
years.p: Amy Farina, who married Alec's brother Ian MacKaye, plays with him in [[The Evens|3a3b3e5d-2d28-4108-875e-30686d2710e8]] and later [[Coriky|d471b090-3866-4cf3-b8a0-476e11f30a58]]. Alec MacKaye sings in [[Hammered Hulls|64368968-d520-49ea-a248-9ccc29e1467f]] and worked as chief preparator at the Phillips Collection in Washington.

sources.title: The Collapsar: No One Like Me, Amy Farina and the Warmers
